correctness.rationale: Every level-n inverse branch maps the unit interval into an affine cylinder of constant Jacobian magnitude, and the diagonal-crossing point is a_w/(1-s_w). Its exact event integral yields an absolutely convergent expansion through signed branch powers. The first three modes and their coefficients were recomputed algebraically; for k>=3 each base has modulus <=p^4+(1-p)^4<1 and the sum of omitted weights is (1-p)^4/p, giving a rigorous all-n error. Comparing |2p-1| and p^3+(1-p)^3 shows spectral crossings at p=1/3 and p=2/3, with signed/modulus distinctions; the latter collision has n times an exponential. Taylor expansions at p=1/3+lambda/n and p=2/3+lambda/n establish the asserted critical windows. A separate exact-rational cylinder enumerator checked 54 cases and 36 independently truncated-series estimates; finite checks are not used as a substitute for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The natural lag-n two-observation order event detects temporally directed rank correlations of deterministic interval dynamics. The result gives a complete asymptotic phase diagram, sign alternation on one parameter side, a double-mode resonance at a separate parameter, and explicit critical windows at scale 1/n; these are not inferable from one-lag autocorrelations or isolated short consecutive order frequencies. Nontrivial analytic remainder estimates make all parameter and lag statements reproducible and falsifiable. The object and quantifiers are motivated by parameter-dependent ordinal time-series analysis rather than arbitrary numerical slices.
